description.narrative:
IMS facilitates public interest journalists, content producers, and media outlets in providing reliable information and inclusive public debate, empowering marginalized communities to participate in public life and claim their rights. IMS works through trust-based partnerships, strategic funding, capacity development, and coalition building, all while promoting diversity, equity, and inclusion, and upholding human rights and digital infrastructure awareness. In contexts of restricted democratic space, IMS aims to bolster the resilience of media actors, while in less restrictive environments, it focuses on sustaining and advancing progress. IMS's approach encompasses enhancing the quality of journalism, reaching diverse audiences, ensuring viability, and addressing safety concerns within supportive legal and policy frameworks. IMS operates across three main outcome areas:
Strategic outcome area 1: Public interest content and business viability - centers on fostering public interest content and ensuring the viability of media businesses. IMS facilitates public interest journalists, content producers, and media outlets in producing fact-based content and engaging with diverse audiences, including marginalized communities. This involves enhancing audience understanding, developing robust business models, and adhering to ethical standards. IMS supports the development of codes of conduct for media partners to ensure content integrity and ethical practices. Assumptions include the willingness of media actors to uphold public interest values, harness online environments effectively, and engage audiences. IMS provides expert input and capacity development, focusing on quality content, combating misinformation, and experimenting with new business models. The organization emphasizes coalition building and coordination, fostering collaboration among partners and like-minded civic groups to amplify the impact of public interest journalism and uphold shared values. IMS states that Strategic outcome 1 is its core outcome, which is supported by outcome 2 and 3.
Strategic outcome 2: Safety of journalists, content producers and media - focuses on ensuring the safety of public interest journalists, content producers, and media, enabling them to work freely. IMS acknowledges the various physical, digital, economic, psychological, and legal challenges these individuals face and adopts a comprehensive approach outlined by "the four Ps": prevention, preparation, protection, and prosecution. Drawing from the UN Plan of Action on the Safety of Journalists, IMS and its partners aim to create sustainable improvements in journalists' safety through local, national, and international engagement. Key focus areas include safeguarding media operations, developing local safety mechanisms, and advocating for international legal frameworks to support free expression. IMS provides expert input and capacity development to support partners in safeguarding media workspaces and facilitates dialogue between stakeholders to develop effective safety mechanisms. Through coalition building and coordination, IMS ensures that partners' experiences inform global discussions and strategic decision-making, thereby advancing safety measures for journalists and media professionals.
Strategic outcome 3: Policy, laws, regulations and public interest infrastructure - The overarching goal is to ensure that public interest journalists, content producers, and media benefit from legislative policy frameworks and digital measures conducive to media viability and free expression, focusing on policy, laws, regulations, and public interest infrastructure. This involves engaging with stakeholders such as states, tech companies, and civil society groups to advocate for legislative reforms, improve economic conditions for media, and establish self-regulatory mechanisms for ethical content production. IMS provides expert input, capacity development, and coalition building to support partners in advocating for policy changes and fostering inclusive collaborations across sectors, with a particular emphasis on gender and inclusiveness in media-related initiatives.

Stöd till International Media Support (IMS) som är internationell NGO som verkar för att främja fri och oberoende media över hela världen. Grundad 2001 och med säte i Köpenhamn, Danmark, verkar IMS globalt för att stärka mediaprofessionellas kapacitet, stödja pressfrihet och främja oberoende journalistik i regioner som står inför utmaningar såsom konflikter, politisk instabilitet och censur. Genom partnerskap med lokala mediaorganisationer, journalister och civilsamhällesgrupper tillhandahåller IMS olika former av stöd, så som utbildning, mentorskap, säkerhetsåtgärder, påverkansarbete och bidrag för att möjliggöra för mediekanaler och praktiker att verka effektivt i svåra miljöer. År 2023 samarbetade IMS med över 200 partners, genomförde 35 program i 26 länder i MENA, Afrika, Asien och Europa.

Support to International Media Support (IMS) that is a non-profit organisation dedicated to promoting free and independent media worldwide. Founded in 2001 and headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, IMS operates globally to strengthen the capacity of media professionals, support press freedom, and foster independent journalism in regions facing challenges such as conflict, political instability, and censorship. Through partnerships with local media organisations, journalists, and civil society groups, IMS provides a range of support including training, mentoring, safety measures, advocacy, and grants to enable media outlets and practitioners to operate effectively in challenging environments. In 2023, IMS collaborated with over 200 partners, implementing 35 programs, across 26 countries in MENA, Africa, Asia, and Europe.

description.narrative:
Outcome 1, Public interest content, audience engagement and media viability
Investigative journalism exposing a ~€160 billion hidden sovereign-debt scheme, Senegal, Togo, Burkina Faso. IMS contributed through direct funding and editorial support to the investigative partner, via the Senegalese journalist Momar Dieng, that traced how an IB Bank debt was allegedly laundered into sovereign debt. The reporting was publicly acknowledged by Senegal's Prime Minister, accelerated legal proceedings, and led the IMF to make full audits and centralised debt management a condition for further support.
Wadaag, Somalia, reshaping ethics in Somali media practice. IMS funded and structurally supported the Wadaag content-sharing platform, providing editorial mentoring and a peace-oriented journalism framework that an external evaluation credited with helping the network "not only influence audiences but also reshape ethics in Somali media practice," strengthening social cohesion in a post-conflict setting.
"No Other Land," 2025 Oscar for Best Documentary Feature. IMS provided direct production and development support to the film starting in 2022, part of its broader documentary-ecosystem work, funding, distribution links, safety support for filmmakers. The film went on to win the Oscar, the European Film Award and the BAFTA.
Outcome 2, Safety of journalists, content producers and media
Zimbabwe's national media policy and sexual-harassment policy. IMS contributed through sustained, multi-year funding and advisory support to MISA Zimbabwe, Media Alliance of Zimbabwe, Gender Media Connect and the Zimbabwe Union of Journalists, backing their lobbying, engagement meetings, conferences and position papers over several years. This support underpinned both the new national policies and a women journalists' protection fund, set up by GMC, that provided redress in a 14-year harassment case. .
Institutionalised national safety mechanisms in Pakistan and Indonesia. IMS contributed through technical advisory support and coalition-building that helped Pakistan operationalise its federal journalist protection commission and helped Indonesia expand its National Press Safety Task Force and formalise cooperation with police and prosecution authorities.
Emergency and mental-health support in Gaza and Ukraine. In Gaza, IMS contributed emergency assistance, improved connectivity and survival supplies, enabling journalists to continue reporting under extreme conditions. In Ukraine, IMS, via Sida top-up funding, supported partner Suspilnist in building a dedicated case-management system giving journalists direct access to mental-health consultations, reaching 51 journalists, 102 hours, in the programme's first month and expanding to 67 journalists, 523 hours, across 18 outlets by April 2026.
Outcome 3, Policy, legal, and digital frameworks enabling public interest media
The Copenhagen Conference on Information Integrity. IMS co-convened and organisationally led the conference together with the Digital Democracy Initiative and the Danish MFA, contributing convening capacity, thematic framing, aligned with the UN Global Principles for Information Integrity, and follow-through into a practical scalable-solutions catalogue and the 2026 "Copenhagen Manual" newsroom resilience tool.
DSA-informed digital governance recommendations for Moldova and Ukraine. IMS convened and managed a High-Level Expert Group, coordinated country-level expert analysis, ensured quality assurance and alignment with EU Digital Services Act frameworks, and translated the findings into a Phase 2 implementation methodology, giving legislators and regulators a practical reference point on systemic digital risks ahead of elections.
Coalition advocacy leading to the release of detained media workers and suspension of Ethiopia's National Internet Gateway rollout. IMS contributed by supporting and helping coordinate the partner coalitions behind this advocacy in Cambodia and Ethiopia, combining evidence-based reporting, legal support and sustained engagement with authorities that produced these two concrete policy reversals..
